title: Square-root noise bound for threshold functions
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a linear threshold function: there are real weights $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ and a real offset $a_0$ such that $f(x)$ is $1$ when $a_0+\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\geq0$ and is $-1$ otherwise. For $0<\delta\leq\tfrac12$, the probability that $f$ changes when each coordinate of a uniformly chosen input is independently flipped with probability $\delta$ is at most $\sqrt{1/m}$, where $m=\lfloor1/\delta\rfloor$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a linear threshold function with real weights and offset
